story:
Field Marshal Nebir has three officers, and the court calls them the Marshal's lieutenants as if there were no other kind. The Marshal chose them himself, which no other office in the court has ever been allowed to do, and Grand Chancellor Adremal wrote their lines under the Marshal's in the Second Roll on the condition that there would never be more than the Marshal could keep at his table. Two of them stand there still, at the war table in High Lord Baln's hall where the whole hollow is cut into black stone and the realms' frontier is cut around the edge; the third lives among the Chthonic Knights.

Gargantan moves the pieces. Loran keeps the count. Between them they are the reason the Marshal is never surprised: Gargantan sets out where everything is, Loran tells him how much of it there is, and Nebir works out what it would take to kill it and where. They are small for officers, the size of the familiars that run the halls, and the host of the south has learned not to laugh. In the Seventh Roll, when the brood of Baln's walls overflowed and Earl Zh'alzhak led it north to the Gate, it was Gargantan who moved the pieces that brought it home in rows, and Loran who counted it back in, short by exactly the number Gatekeeper Dommel had charged.

The third officer is the Marshal's eye. After the feud of the Blade and the Hook, Nebir asked each of the three orders to keep one of his officers in its house, so that he would never again learn of a war from the dead. The Mutilators refused. The Inquisition said it would be glad to, and would of course examine the officer first, and the Marshal withdrew the offer. Only Prince Abdin's knights agreed, and Lieutenant Persun has lived in their chapter house since. He writes to the Marshal. The knights know he writes. They have never asked to read the letters, and Persun has never offered, and the arrangement has held for six Rolls on that understanding.

The realms' oldest maps name a fourth, Commander Abgar, beside Persun in the knights' house. The court has an account of that too: Abgar was called to the war table in the Ninth Roll, when Prince Abdin first began work on the Army of Shadows, and did not come back to the house, and his place there is kept empty. The Marshal does not speak of him. Loran, asked how many officers the Marshal has, says three, and does not hesitate, which in Loran is the same as an answer.

The realms each have a word for the lieutenants. Albion's sergeants say the Marshal's officers are the only demons who would understand a muster roll. Midgard's huscarls say a war-chief is only as good as the men who tell him the truth, and that the Marshal has two. Hibernia's druids, who distrust counting, say the small ones at the table are more dangerous than the Marshal, because the Marshal only decides, and they are the ones who know.
legend: Gargantan and Loran stand at the Field Marshal's war table at the south end of Baln's hall, within a couple of hundred units of Nebir, so expect all three together; they are level 68 and go down faster than the Marshal, so kill them first. Persun is the odd one out: he is in the Chthonic Knights' chapter house in the north-west, a 68 among the knights, and you meet him while clearing the house. All three are plain melee with no scripts and respawn in about three minutes, so the table lieutenants can come back on you if the Marshal fight drags. Players call Gargantan and Loran the clerks, and old guides list a Commander Abgar next to Persun who is not in this world at all.

loremasterTopic.text: Field Marshal [Nebir]'s three officers: Gargantan, who moves the pieces at the war table; Loran, who keeps the count; and Persun, the Marshal's eye in the [Chthonic Knights]' chapter house. The old maps name a Commander Abgar, whose place in the house is kept empty.

bookPage: From a Midgard skald's account of the war table, kept at Jordheim: There were two small ones at the table, no taller than a dog on its hind legs, and the great one stood behind them and said nothing. The first moved stones on the table without looking up. The second spoke numbers, one after another, in a voice like a man reckoning a debt. I knew some of the numbers. One was the count of our war-band at the stair. One was the count of us still standing. The second number changed while I listened, and the small one said it again, smaller, without looking at us at all.
bookPages: From a Midgard skald's account of the war table, kept at Jordheim: There were two small ones at the table, no taller than a dog on its hind legs, and the great one stood behind them and said nothing. The first moved stones on the table without looking up. The second spoke numbers, one after another, in a voice like a man reckoning a debt. I knew some of the numbers. One was the count of our war-band at the stair. One was the count of us still standing. The second number changed while I listened, and the small one said it again, smaller, without looking at us at all.

The skald went on: Later, in the black knights' house, we found a third officer, who was not a knight and who stood among them as a stranger stands at a feast. He fought us as they did. When he fell he said a few words that were plainly meant for someone else, as if he had been writing them in his head for a long time. Beside him was an empty place on the floor, kept clear, with a mark cut into the stone. Our scout, who reads a little of their scratches, said it was a name, and a rank higher than his.

members.name: Lieutenant Gargantan
members.post: the Field Marshal's war table, Baln's hall
members.story: Gargantan is the Marshal's hand at the war table. He moves the pieces: the stones of three colours that stand on the frontier cut into the table's edge, and the pieces of the court's own host on the hollow cut into its top. He has moved them for ten Rolls without once being told he was wrong, and a Midgard skald who watched him swore he moved one the right way before word of the frontier reached the hollow.

aggro: A piece moves. You were that piece.
death: Move me... to the edge of the table...

members.name: Lieutenant Loran
members.post: the Field Marshal's war table, Baln's hall
members.story: Loran keeps the count. Every number the Marshal works with passes through Loran first: the host of the south, the knights at the east arch, the mortals the Gate reports, the dead. Loran writes nothing down, and has never yet forgotten a number, and the Marshal trusts nobody else to tell him how many. Loran is said to have counted Director Kobil's Army of Shadows once, and to have refused ever since to say the number.
